'''Garry John Tee''' (28 March 1932 – 18 February 2024) was a New Zealand mathematician and [[computer scientist]].

== Biography ==
Garry John Tee was born in [[Whanganui]] on 28 March 1932.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Garry TEE Obituary (2024) |url=https://notices.nzherald.co.nz/nz/obituaries/nzherald-nz/name/garry-tee-obituary?id=54450400 |access-date=2024-11-11 |website=The New Zealand Herald}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Butcher |first1=John |last2=Keam |first2=Ron |date=April 1992 |title=Garry John Tee |url=https://nzmathsoc.org.nz/downloads/profiles/NZMSprofile54_Garry_Tee.pdf?t=1262766191 |journal=New Zealand Mathematics Society Newsletter |volume=54}}</ref> Tee attended [[Auckland University of Technology|Seddon Memorial Technical College]] (now Auckland University of Technology). In 1954, he was awarded a [[Master of Science]] with First Class Honours at the [[University of Auckland|Auckland University College]] (now the University of Auckland).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tee |first=Gary J. |title=From monsters to micros |url=https://history.itp.nz/part-3/tee.html |access-date=2024-11-11 |website=From Yesterday to Tomorrow: 60 years of tech in New Zealand}}</ref> Following graduating, Tee worked as a computer in Australia for an oil prospecting team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Garry Tee |url=https://www.nasa.gov/history/alsj/garytee.html |access-date=2024-11-11 |website=www.nasa.gov}}</ref>

In 1958, Tee was a mathematician at the [[English Electric Company]], contributing to the programming of the [[DEUCE computer]].<ref name=":1" /> In 1964, Tee helped establish the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of Lancaster]] and spent 1965 as a [[visiting scholar]] at the Department of Computer Science, [[Stanford University]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> By 1968, Tee had returned to the Department of Mathematics at the University of Auckland, playing a key role in founding its Department of Computer Science.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Dr Garry Tee |url=https://profiles.auckland.ac.nz/gtee003 |access-date=2024-11-11 |website=The University of Auckland}}</ref> Starting in 1969, Tee was also an active member of the Auckland University Underwater Club.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Recollections – Dr Garry J. Tee |url=https://unidive.co.nz/about/archives/recollections-dr-garry-j-tee/ |access-date=2024-11-11 |website=unidive.co.nz |language=en}}</ref>

In 1971, Tee pursued further studies under [[Richard Bellman]] at the [[University of Southern California]].<ref name=":1" /> However, Bellman's illness and subsequent death led Tee to return to Auckland without completing his doctorate.<ref name=":1" /> In 2003, Tee received an honorary doctorate from the [[Auckland University of Technology]].<ref name=":0" /> 

Tee died in [[Auckland]] on 18 February 2024.<ref name=":0" />

== Publications ==
Tee published widely on numerical analysis, [[Charles Babbage]], early women in mathematics and computing, and history of mathematics, computer science, and science more broadly.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=8 March 2024 |title=Computer pioneer was a familiar figure on the ferry |url=https://museum.cs.auckland.ac.nz/misc/GarryTee-DevonportFlagstaff.html |access-date=2024-11-11 |website=The Devonport Flagstaff}}</ref> Publications include:

* Tee, Garry J. "A novel finite-difference approximation to the biharmonic operator." ''The Computer Journal'' 6, no. 2 (1963): 177–192.
* Tee, Garry J. "Evidence for the Chinese Origin of the Jaguar Motif in Chavin Art".<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/42927974|title=Evidence for the Chinese Origin of the Jaguar Motif in Chavin Art|author=Tee, Garry J.|year=1978|journal=Asian Perspectives|volume=21|issue=1|pages=27–29|jstor=42927974 }}</ref> ''Asian Perspectives'' 21, no. 1 (1978): 27–29.
* Tee, Garry J. "The Heritage of Charles Babbage in Australasia." ''Annals of the History of Computing'' 5, no. 1 (1983): 45–60.
* Tee, Garry J. "A Calendar of the Correspondence of Charles Darwin, 1821–1882." ''Journal of the Royal Society of New Zealand'' 15, no. 3 (1985): 341–343.
* Tee, Garry J. "Mathematics in the Pacific Basin".<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/4026960|title=Mathematics in the Pacific Basin|author=Tee, Garry J.|year=1988|journal=The British Journal for the History of Science|volume=21|issue=4|pages=401–417|doi=10.1017/S0007087400025322 |jstor=4026960 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> ''The British Journal for the History of Science'' 21, no. 4 (1988): 401–417.
* Tee, Garry J. "A Note on Bechmann's Approximate Construction of π, Suggested by a Deleted Sketch in Villard de Honnecourt's Manuscript.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/4026662|title=A Note on Bechmann's Approximate Construction of π, Suggested by a Deleted Sketch in Villard de Honnecourt's Manuscript|author=Tee, Garry J.|year=1989|journal=The British Journal for the History of Science|volume=22|issue=2|pages=241–242|doi=10.1017/S0007087400026017 |jstor=4026662 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>" ''The British Journal for the History of Science'' 22, no. 2 (1989): 241–242.
* Tee, Garry J. "Prime powers of zeros of monic polynomials with integer coefficients." ''The Fibonacci Quarterly'' 32, no. 3 (1994): 277–283.
* Tee, Garry J. "Relics of Davy and Faraday in New Zealand".<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/532079|title=Relics of Davy and Faraday in New Zealand|author=Tee, Garry J.|year=1998|journal=Notes and Records of the Royal Society of London|volume=52|issue=1|pages=93–102|doi=10.1098/rsnr.1998.0037 |jstor=532079 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> ''Notes and Records of the Royal Society of London'' 52, no. 1 (1998): 93–102.
* Tee, Garry J. "Math Bite: Further Generalizations of a Curiosity That Feynman Remembered All His Life.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/2691313|title=Math Bite: Further Generalizations of a Curiosity That Feynman Remembered All His Life|author=Tee, Garry J.|year=1999|journal=Mathematics Magazine|volume=72|issue=1|page=44|doi=10.1080/0025570X.1999.11996697 |jstor=2691313 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>" ''Mathematics Magazine'' 72, no. 1 (1999): 44.
* Tee, Garry J. "Eigenvectors of block circulant and alternating circulant matrices." ''New Zealand Journal of Mathematics'' 36, no. 8 (2007): 195–211.
